claim: Kinabalu Basin fill rests on the Borneo (Crocker) accretionary wedge and its seaward flank — upper plate of the collision system; it is a group of wedge-top/foreland depocentres.
DRU (13.5–12.5 Ma) marks post-collision uplift, major erosion and onset of Stage IV progradation in this province; DRU is distinct from BMU/Top-Crocker (~base Miocene).
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay 2026-09-30 + public mobile-shale dating

claim: 2026 Stage IV NN calibration (IVG NN19 → IVA mid-NN5, intra-IVE E1–E3 at NN11A/NN11B/NN15) is preliminary; NN zones do not equal surfaces — surfaces need seismic-stratal criteria plus age brackets.
Stage III correlation across the Sabah Trough is on HOLD until a dip line with a well tie physically crosses the trough.
At depth, part of the Kinabalu substrate is stacked above underthrust Dangerous Grounds extended crust continuing SE beneath Neogene Borneo sediments.
